216178.overview:
In B-1 Nuclear Bomber, you have to "fly" a B-1 bomber to its destination, and destroy the target of the mission.

You input text commands to control your bomber's altitude, course, radar, weapons, and so on. And, of course, the USSR will try to stop you from bombing their targets, with an arsenal of MiGs and SAMs, and they are dealt with by the use of electronic counter-measures, evasive actions, or by shooting them down.

The game ends when it reaches a logical conclusion, either by deploying your bombs and getting far enough away, returning to base, or being destroyed. After this, you get a short summary, and an option to play again.

The TRS-80, Apple II, and Commodore PET versions were all sold on the same cassette.

313213.overview: Ball Turret Gunner is a game with a first person view where you need to gun down enemy vessels (that look suspiciously like Tie Fighters). You have a direction indicator that tells you where the enemy vessel is coming from, and you can rotate your turret a full 360 degrees. However, your laser takes a long time to recharge, so you must aim carefully and not waste your shots.

326852.overview:
Batter Up!!: A Microbaseball Game is a 2-player arcade-themed baseball game for the TRS-80.

Gameplay takes place primarily from a black and white side-view, featuring a batter and pitcher. The two players take turns throwing pitches, where the pitcher can control the height and speed of the pitch. If the batter comes in contact with the pitch, the details of the action are automatically calculated, and the number of bases, or whether runs are scored is calculated without player control of outfielders.

Game details, including: inning, hits, runs, and score are all displayed on the bottom of the screen during pitching/batting. Players create their team names at the beginning of each session, and all players have the same statistics. A complete game consists of 9 innings, and extra innings if applicable.

326864.overview: June 6, 1944. The start of D-Day. Depending on your choice you will either lead or face the largest amphibious force ever assembled. As the Supreme Allied Commander your job is to establish beachheads on Utah, Omaha, Juno, Gold and Sword, consolidate them, then move out to capture the strategic towns of Cherbourg and Caen, the roadnet at St. Lo, penetrate as deeply as possible into the continent and destroy and disrupt enemy formations. As the German Commander your hope for victory is to deploy your land forces and powerful panzers and contain the enemy and drive him back to the beaches. Either way you have until noon on June 30th (25 days) to accomplish your mission at which time your position will be evaluated. This game provides for solitaire play as the Americans and provides the player with several levels of difficulty.

342638.overview:
What other game lets you interact with Houdini, Picasso, and Merlin, and even get them to talk to each other? These mental patients may only believe that they're Houdini, Picasso, and Merlin, but they can help you get out, and that is your sole objective in this text adventure.

You wake up in a locked mental ward and your wits, a few objects, and the other occupants (inmates, staff, and inmates pretending to be staff) are the resources you must pool to escape. Whom can you trust, and what your route to freedom is, changes with each new game.

In this basic text adventure you use commands like GO WEST or GET THE KEY. You can shorten direction commands to WEST or NORTH (or even W or N if you prefer).

343017.overview: You play as a bee who can move in 4 cardinal directions. On the bottom of the screen is a spider, who will attempt to move underneath the bee and eat it. If the bee gets too close, the spider can eat it. The goal is to try to sting the spider before it can eat you. The game keeps track of how many times the spider or the bee has won.

343290.overview: Blitzkrieg is a fairly simple game where you control a man who can run left and right horizontally across the bottom of the screen. He needs to avoid up to 15 bombs falling simultaneously from above. You have three lives. The bombs become faster as the game progresses.

364725.overview:
This is the first chapter in the Maces & Magic series.

You equip a character of your own creation and journey into a weird world of dank dungeons and fiery dragons. This fantasy adventure features one of the largest databases ever created for a microcomputer role-playing game.

A real challenge!

371698.overview:
A turn-based strategy wargame set at the dawn of the US civil war, recreating the first major clash between the Confederate army and Grant's forces.

The game is played from an hexagonal grid and divided on turns of movement and attack phases, with pre-defined units divided in regiments of different sizes and abilities. You can choose whether to lead the Confederate or Union forces and the game allows for single or "hot-seat" 2P-multiplayer modes.

371944.overview: On December 16, 1944 in the twilight of the Third Reich, Hitler played his last desperate gamble and launched a massive surprise assault against the thin allied lines in the Ardennes forest of Belgium and Luxembourg. As the German Commander your goal is to cross the Ardennes forest and get to the other side of the Meuse River. With division/regiment sized forces you must storm thru the allied forces taking as many towns as possible. If you choose to command the allied forces your goal is the same as the American commander in 1944. Hold out against the attacking Germans until reinforcements arrive while keeping the enemy from taking towns and exiting from the map. The game lasts 15 turns. Each turn historically representing one day. The game can be played solitaire or against another individual.

383740.overview:
Basketball is a 1 - 2 player basketball game for the TRS-80.

A 1 on 1 basketball game, where each basket is worth 2 points. Each game is 5 minutes in length, and there are 5 levels of computer difficulty. Two players can also compete for basketball dominance. Players can take the ball from their opponent, and can take a shot on the basket when close.

383773.overview:
Bridge Partner is a 1-player simulation of the card game bridge.

A game designed to allow a player to train their bridge skill. It is entirely text based, and all commands are inputted via text prompt. The computer deals at least 10 million different hands. The player and dummy player compete against the computer in regular contract bridge. Or the player can use the dealer subprogram to specify a criterion for high card points and Bridge Partner will deal four new hands. The player can create customized hands to practice, and can save specific hands for future replay. This even allows Bridge Partner to test itself against the bridge game from the local newspaper.

Later releases of the game featured an implementation of 3D Tictactoe on a 4x4x4 grid to fill up the remaining space on the tape.

383774.overview:
Bounceoids is a science-fiction themed arcade game for the TRS-80.

Gameplay is similar to the more famous Asteroids, where the player controls a small ship which can rotate 360 degrees and fire forwards. The ship can accelerate to move, and also has a shield which can offer temporary invincibility. The player must shoot a variety of asteroids and alien menaces. There are a total of 10 difficulty levels which control the size, shape, and speed of asteroids. The player starts with 3 ships, and the skill level increases and a new ship is awarded every 10,000 points. Every 20,000 points brings on a bonus stage.

417686.overview:
The Battle of Zeighty is a single-player strategy game.

Congratulations! You have just been appointed general of a small and struggling army, in a small and struggling country. You should consider this an honor, even though the army has had six generals in the last two months. Somehow, each general seemed to mysteriously disappear after a battle was lost.

To defeat the enemy nation, you must conquer The Zeighty Pass, a highly defended pass through an otherwise impassable mountain range, and the sole supply route for the enemy's advanced troops. If the pass can be conquered, the tide of war will turn in your nation's favor.

The player arranges an army of 10 units, which can be chosen from armored infantry, tanks, mine layers, and artillery. Armored infantry and takes serve as combat troops, while artillery can bombard enemy positions from a distance. Mine layers can deploy mines to destroy enemy units. Gameplay occurs on a battlefield, where the player can move their units in 8 directions, and issue attack commands. The player controls a home base, which must be defended, and fog of war allows enemy units to hide when at a sufficient range. Each unit starts with 1000 health units, and will progressively take damage during combat until they are destroyed. Victory is achieved by destroying the enemy's base to the north.

417696.overview:
Creative Computing Board Games-1 is a compilation of several games for TRS-80:

* Backgammon - A version of the classic game, programmed by Scott Adams
* Qubic - a 4-D Tic Tac Toe implementation
* Flip Disc - an Othello/Reversi implementation
* Wumpus I and Wumpus II - two versions of Hunt the Wumpus
* Mugwump - the classic type-in BASIC game

462108.overview:
Back-40 is an early black and white translation of the board game for the TRS-80.

Written in machine code, it allows for only 1-player versus computer game play. The board is graphically displayed, and the player uses text input to place moves. The player is always represented by white, while the computer is striped. Only legal moves are allowed. Dice throws are displayed on the right hand side of the screen.

462295.overview: Battleground is a war simulation for two players taking place in World War 2 (specifically, Berlin in 1944). One player takes the role of the American commander moving toward Berlin, and the other player takes the role of the German commander planning a defense. Players take turns selecting their troops and associated items (such as bunkers) and then placing them on the battlefield. Once that process is complete, combat is turn-based. There are two types of combat commands - movement and firing.
